# ACC012 `sequential-device-loop`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A loop in an OpenACC compute region runs sequentially: the compiler found a loop-carried dependence.

## Why

In a `kernels` region the compiler parallelises only the loops it can prove independent. A loop-carried
dependence (`y(i) = y(i) + y(i-1)`) makes it generate a serial kernel: the loop runs on one GPU thread,
often slower than on the host. Restructure the computation (a scan, a different loop order), or move
the loop off the device; if the dependence is only apparent (aliasing the compiler cannot rule out),
say so with `!$acc loop independent`.
Reported only with `fobis lint --compiler-feedback LOG` (see the linting guide).

## Reported

```fortran
!$acc kernels
do i = 2, n
  y(i) = y(i) + y(i-1)      ! nvfortran: Loop carried dependence of y prevents parallelization
end do
!$acc end kernels
```

## Preferred

```fortran
!$acc parallel loop independent   ! only when the dependence is not real
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[ACC012] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = ACC012` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).
